no-kill-by-name.message: Do not kill by name (pkill, killall): it can match your own shell or an innocent process. To find a process, run `pgrep -xl <name>` as its own command, read the PID, confirm it is the right process, then `kill <pid>`.

no-pgrep-substitution.description: Never capture pgrep output in $(...) or backticks.
no-pgrep-substitution.message: Do not use pgrep inside $(...) or backticks: a name lookup can match your own shell or an innocent process. Instead, run `pgrep -xl <name>` as its own command, read the PID, confirm it is the right process, then `kill <pid>`.

no-pgrep-pipeline.description: Never pipe pgrep into other commands.
no-pgrep-pipeline.message: Do not pipe pgrep into other commands (kill via xargs, head, wc, ...): it hides which process is about to be hit. Instead, run `pgrep -xl <name>` as its own command, read the PID, confirm it is the right process, then `kill <pid>`.

no-pgrep-status.description: Never use pgrep's exit status (&&, ||, !, if, while, until, watch).
no-pgrep-status.message: Do not use pgrep's exit status in &&, ||, !, if, while, until or watch: it can match your own shell and never turns false. To wait for a process to exit, poll `kill -0 <pid>` with a PID you already identified.

no-kill-lookup-substitution.description: Never kill PIDs produced by ps, pidof or lsof inside $(...).
no-kill-lookup-substitution.message: Do not kill PIDs produced by ps, pidof or lsof inside $(...) or backticks: the lookup result is not checked before it is signalled. Instead, run the lookup as its own command, confirm the PID, then `kill <pid>`.

no-kill-lookup-xargs.description: Never feed `xargs kill` from ps, pidof or lsof.
no-kill-lookup-xargs.message: Do not feed `xargs kill` from ps, pidof or lsof: the PIDs are not checked before they are signalled. Instead, run the lookup as its own command, confirm the PID, then `kill <pid>`.

warn-pgrep-in-loop.description: pgrep inside a loop: fine for reading, not for deciding.
warn-pgrep-in-loop.message: pgrep inside a loop: make sure you only read its output. Do not loop on it to wait for a process or to choose what to signal. To wait for a process to exit, poll `kill -0 <pid>` with a PID you already identified.

warn-pgrep-full-cmdline.description: pgrep -f matches full command lines, including your own shell.
warn-pgrep-full-cmdline.message: `pgrep -f` matches full command lines, including your own shell and pgrep itself. Prefer `pgrep -xl <name>` (exact process name).

catch: if pgrep -q x; then echo y; fi
if ! pgrep x; then y; fi
while pgrep x; do sleep 1; done
until pgrep -q x; do sleep 1; done
until ! pgrep x; do sleep 1; done
pass:
cat <<'EOF'
if pgrep x; then :; fi
EOF
if true; then pgrep -xl x; fi
while true; do pgrep -xl x; sleep 1; done

catch: ps aux | grep x | awk '{print $2}' | xargs kill
while true; do pgrep -xl x; sleep 1; done
for i in 1 2 3; do pgrep -xl x; done
until false; do pgrep -xl x; done
while sleep 1; do pgrep -xl x; done
pass: if true; then pgrep -xl x; fi

cat <<'EOF'
while true; do pgrep x; done
EOF
